recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Future editors may remove the commented-out old search example during ordinary page cleanup, but no FHIR-36098 source correction is needed now.
issue_request: FHIR-36098 asked to replace the old Search via Messaging mapping of search parameters into typed Parameters because that mapping lost REST search behavior such as decimal values, prefixes, modifiers, URI version syntax, and joins. The approved resolution says messaging search that mirrors REST should use a Parameters instance with a standard parameter named "url" and a valueString containing the search string normally to the right of the base URL, with MessageHeader event search-type or search-system.
initial_application: Commit f3dfec64462aa8ec3a0d95db4cf9eff7ace9394e applied the decision to source/messaging.html by adding the url/valueString guidance and commenting out the older typed-parameter mapping table and example. Commit 4baa8f22bae6d8f787c024219b5842a6cc658bb5 later made only XML fragment quote fixes in the same area. No later source commit was found that reversed the FHIR-36098 semantics.
additional_context: source/navigation.xml lists Messaging under the Implementation section, confirming source/messaging.html is a current build-scoped narrative page. The current visible Invoking Search via Messages section contains the approved url/valueString, Patient?name=joe, search-type/search-system, CapabilityStatement, and alternative-mechanism guidance. The old resourceType mapping remains only in an HTML comment. Related FHIR-36116 was resolved Resolved - No Change/Not Persuasive because FHIR-36098 made that old resourceType text no longer relevant. The linked Zulip thread confirms FHIR-36098 and FHIR-36116 came from the same Search in Messaging review; the Confluence minutes found only record assignment and do not conflict with the later Jira vote.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current implementer-visible source already matches the approved Jira resolution, and deleting hidden commented historical text would be editorial cleanup rather than a necessary current-spec correction.
